name: Tropical aroid / chunky mix
light: Bright indirect to medium indirect light; protect from harsh midday sun indoors.
water: Water when the top 30-50% of mix dries; do not leave standing in water.
humidity: Average indoor humidity is usually workable; 50-70% helps larger leaves and velvety species.
soil: Chunky, airy aroid mix with potting soil/coco plus orchid bark, perlite, or pumice.
airflow: Gentle airflow helps reduce fungal issues; avoid cold drafts and heater vents.

name: Rare/velvety aroid
light: Bright filtered light; avoid direct sun on thin or velvety leaves.
water: Keep evenly moist but never soggy; allow the upper mix to begin drying between waterings.
humidity: High humidity preferred, often 60-80%, with steady warmth.
soil: Very airy aroid mix with bark, perlite/pumice, coco chips, and a moisture-retentive component.
airflow: High humidity should be paired with airflow to prevent leaf spotting and rot.

name: Low-light resilient foliage
light: Low to bright indirect light; growth is faster with brighter indirect light.
water: Let soil dry well between waterings; overwatering is the main risk.
humidity: Normal household humidity is fine.
soil: Well-draining indoor potting mix with perlite or pumice.
airflow: Tolerates normal indoor air; avoid cold drafts.

name: Bright-light ficus/tree-form houseplant
light: Bright indirect light with some gentle direct sun if acclimated.
water: Water when the top 25-40% of soil dries; keep routine consistent.
humidity: Average humidity works, but avoid very dry air.
soil: Rich, well-draining potting mix; avoid compacted wet soil.
airflow: Avoid cold drafts and sudden moves; many ficus drop leaves after abrupt changes.

name: Prayer plant / calathea humidity-sensitive foliage
light: Medium to bright indirect light; avoid direct sun that fades or scorches leaves.
water: Keep lightly and evenly moist; avoid fully drying out or staying soggy.
humidity: Prefers higher humidity, often 50-70%; sensitive to dry air.
soil: Moisture-retentive but draining mix with coco/peat and perlite.
airflow: Avoid cold drafts, hot vents, and stagnant wet foliage.

name: Alocasia / elephant-ear tropical
light: Bright indirect light; some morning sun can work after acclimation.
water: Keep evenly moist during growth, letting the top layer dry; reduce watering in dormancy.
humidity: Moderate to high humidity, ideally 50-70%.
soil: Chunky but moisture-retentive mix; avoid dense wet soil around corms.
airflow: Good airflow helps prevent pests and fungal spots in humid setups.

name: Indoor palm / tropical floor plant
light: Bright indirect to medium light depending on species.
water: Keep slightly moist but not waterlogged; many palms dislike drying completely.
humidity: Average to higher humidity; brown tips often worsen in dry air.
soil: Well-draining palm or indoor potting mix.
airflow: Avoid cold drafts and hot dry vents.

name: Begonia / flowering foliage tropical
light: Bright indirect light; some morning sun can help flowering.
water: Let the top layer dry, then water thoroughly; avoid wet leaves and soggy roots.
humidity: Average to moderate humidity; airflow matters more than misting.
soil: Light, well-draining potting mix.
airflow: Good airflow prevents powdery mildew and leaf spotting.

name: Flowering potted plant
light: Bright indirect light; some gentle sun supports blooms.
water: Keep evenly moist while blooming, then adjust for dormancy or rest period.
humidity: Average indoor humidity works for most.
soil: Quality potting mix with drainage.
airflow: Avoid hot vents; remove spent blooms and yellow leaves.

name: Succulent / dryland plant
light: Very bright light; many need several hours of direct sun or strong grow light.
water: Soak thoroughly, then let mix dry completely before watering again.
humidity: Low to average humidity is fine.
soil: Fast-draining cactus/succulent mix with pumice, perlite, or grit.
airflow: Good airflow and dry leaves/crowns help prevent rot.

name: Cactus / arid desert plant
light: High light with direct sun after acclimation.
water: Water deeply but infrequently; keep mostly dry, especially in cool months.
humidity: Low humidity preferred.
soil: Mineral-heavy cactus mix with excellent drainage.
airflow: Strong airflow and fast drying reduce rot risk.

name: Hoya / epiphytic succulent vine
light: Bright indirect light; some gentle direct sun supports flowering.
water: Let mix dry partly to mostly between waterings; avoid heavy wet soil.
humidity: Average humidity works; higher humidity helps growth.
soil: Airy epiphyte mix with orchid bark, perlite/pumice, and light organic matter.
airflow: Good airflow supports healthy vines and reduces fungal issues.

name: Epiphytic orchid
light: Bright filtered light; avoid hot direct sun unless the species prefers it.
water: Water when bark/moss approaches dry; never keep roots stagnant.
humidity: Moderate to high humidity with airflow.
soil: Orchid bark, sphagnum, mounted culture, or species-appropriate epiphyte media.
airflow: Air movement is critical around roots and leaves.

name: Moisture-loving fern
light: Medium to bright indirect light; avoid hot direct sun.
water: Keep evenly moist, not soggy; avoid drying completely.
humidity: High humidity preferred; dry air causes crisp fronds.
soil: Moist, organic, well-draining fern mix.
airflow: Gentle airflow helps prevent disease while retaining humidity.

name: Air plant / tillandsia
light: Bright indirect light with some gentle morning sun.
water: Soak or rinse regularly, then dry fully within a few hours.
humidity: Average to moderate humidity.
soil: No soil; mount in a breathable display.
airflow: Very important: plants must dry after watering.

name: Carnivorous bog plant
light: Very bright light; many need direct sun.
water: Keep consistently wet with distilled/rain/RO water; avoid tap water minerals.
humidity: Average to high depending on species; airflow still matters.
soil: Nutrient-poor peat/sphagnum and perlite/sand; never fertilized potting soil.
airflow: Use airflow to prevent mold in wet media.

name: Mediterranean herb
light: Full sun outdoors or the brightest indoor window/grow light.
water: Let the top soil dry; avoid constant wet roots.
humidity: Average to low humidity; prefers airflow.
soil: Lean, very well-draining mix; add perlite, pumice, or sand.
airflow: Excellent airflow improves flavor and reduces mildew.

name: Leafy culinary herb
light: Bright light to full sun; some afternoon shade in hot climates.
water: Keep evenly moist but not soggy; containers dry quickly.
humidity: Average humidity is fine.
soil: Rich potting mix or garden soil with good drainage.
airflow: Airflow reduces mildew and fungus gnats.

name: Fruiting vegetable / edible starter
light: Full sun, ideally 6+ hours outdoors or strong grow light.
water: Consistent watering; avoid drought stress and waterlogged roots.
humidity: Average outdoor humidity; airflow is important.
soil: Rich, fertile, well-draining soil or container mix.
airflow: Good spacing and airflow reduce disease.

name: Outdoor flowering annual
light: Full sun to part sun depending on species.
water: Water when the top soil dries; containers may need frequent watering.
humidity: Outdoor humidity is fine; avoid crowded stagnant plantings.
soil: Fertile, well-draining garden or container mix.
airflow: Spacing and deadheading help reduce disease and prolong bloom.

name: Outdoor perennial
light: Match species to full sun, part sun, or shade.
water: Water to establish; many need less once rooted.
humidity: Outdoor humidity is fine.
soil: Well-draining garden soil amended for the species.
airflow: Good spacing reduces fungal pressure.

name: Flowering shrub / landscape plant
light: Usually part sun to full sun; check species and climate.
water: Deep watering while establishing; then species-appropriate irrigation.
humidity: Outdoor humidity is fine; choose climate-appropriate plants.
soil: Garden soil matched to species pH/drainage needs.
airflow: Prune/space for airflow and bloom performance.

name: Citrus / fruiting container tree
light: Full sun outdoors; brightest possible indoor overwintering light.
water: Water deeply when the upper soil dries; avoid soggy roots.
humidity: Average outdoor humidity; indoors avoid hot dry vents.
soil: Fast-draining citrus/cactus-style container mix.
airflow: Outdoor airflow helps pests/disease; indoor trees need inspection for scale/mites.

name: Bonsai / small tree in shallow pot
light: Very bright light; outdoor species should live outdoors.
water: Check often; shallow pots dry quickly but should not stay waterlogged.
humidity: Species-specific; indoor bonsai dislike dry hot vents.
soil: Bonsai mix with akadama/pumice/lava or species-appropriate gritty mix.
airflow: Outdoor airflow is ideal for many bonsai.

name: Outdoor palm / sun-loving landscape palm
light: Full sun is best; young plants can appreciate a gentler transition if moved from shade or indoors.
water: Water regularly while establishing, then deeply and less often once rooted; avoid constantly soggy soil.
humidity: Outdoor humidity is fine; good airflow helps keep crowns and fronds healthy.
soil: Fast-draining ground or large-container soil; avoid standing water around the crown.
airflow: Outdoor airflow is beneficial; remove crowded dead material and avoid burying the crown.

name: Outdoor conifer / specimen tree
light: Full sun to part sun depending on climate and plant age; avoid dark and crowded siting.
water: Water consistently while establishing, then shift to deeper, less frequent watering in well-draining soil.
humidity: Outdoor humidity is fine; avoid prolonged stagnant wet foliage where fungal issues linger.
soil: Well-draining ground soil with room for roots; avoid sites that stay waterlogged.
airflow: Good spacing and airflow support strong branching and reduce fungal pressure.
